patches.detail: On the timber deck/diagonal rail only, remove small angular color steps crossing the normal grain. Keep all plank gaps and cast shadows.
Remove the broad jagged orange/yellow patch divide across the large vertical post. Continue each existing vertical wood plane and highlight smoothly through the cut.
Remove the conspicuous joined sawtooth light/dark boundary across the large post and front horizontal timber beam; keep the real diagonal cast shadow unchanged.

Make support timber shading continuous across olive/violet splice, repair the tiny beam paint step and the local cyan ring/water tone join. Preserve exact support silhouette, ring ellipse and original reflection.

The open water to the RIGHT OF THE WOOD POST contains an erroneous sawtooth horizon around local y=550..630. ERASE that entire jagged contour. It is a stitching defect, NOT a reflection or real shadow. Repaint water throughout local x=570..1254,y=400..800 as one uninterrupted smooth blue gradient from the current upper cyan-blue into current lower cobalt-blue; no hard boundary anywhere. Repair the local brown/violet split in the curved support band at local x=250..570,y=470..620, preserving the structural band shape.

ERASE the entire erroneous mountain-shaped sawtooth contour across local y=480..700. It is not real geometry or water reflection. Repaint that transition as one uninterrupted smooth blue gradient from the existing upper cyan-blue into the lower cobalt-blue. No discernible border, no straight seam, no shadow silhouette. Preserve the genuine faint broad water planes at very top and bottom.

ERASE the polygonal angular blue patch boundary across the open water at local x=160..665,y=390..550; it is a stitching defect, NOT a real cast shadow. Repaint smooth current-blue water throughout that small area, matching both sides without any border. Repair the horizontal jagged lighting split across the large right wooden post near local y=400, making its wood grain continuous vertically while keeping the round base outline and water ring exactly.

ERASE the erroneous vertical jagged color boundary approximately local x=350..510,y=250..770 and the small hard triangular fragment at x=490..570,y=390..460. These are stitching defects, NOT genuine reflection geometry. Restore the actual left post reflection contour from image2 while keeping image1 palette. Blend its faint lower reflection naturally into water; the large right post reflection and both water rings stay fixed. Smooth blue water should connect from left to right without a visible vertical division.

ERASE the erroneous vertical sawtooth color division at local x=360..455,y=500..1080. This is a stitching defect NOT an actual reflection. Paint an uninterrupted smooth blue gradient across that water region so left and right unite naturally, without adding any shapes. Keep genuine upper post reflections unchanged. The same splice cuts the bottom rail at local x=400..470,y=1080..1254: make the wood highlight and warm shadow paint continuous there while preserving all rail contours and existing woodgrain.

Repair jagged highlight/shadow patch crossing the diagonal foreground rail and shaded front face. Match continuous wood grain and illumination while preserving every rail edge. Bottom physical tile edge may be repaired.

Repair small angular paint/color division on bottom horizontal wooden rail. Preserve the actual segmented joint and the nearby upright post. Do not alter open water. Bottom physical tile edge may be repaired.
